1.Sub-event_summary: At the end of August 1944, Allied forces pursued multiple objectives including securing Channel ports, neutralizing V-weapons, liberating regions, and destroying enemy forces, with the primary goal being the Rhine River. Commanders believed a Rhine crossing could capture the Ruhr and end the war, given the disintegrating German military. The First Army G-2 highlighted critical German situations depriving hope, questioning how long control could be maintained. Threatened by Soviet advances, Germans appeared unable to stand short of the West Wall, suggesting withdrawal and repairs there.

5.Sub-event_summary: Recognizing Germans could only resist at Albert-Meuse line, Bradley shifted from Rhine to blocking retreat, turning First Army north to cut Lille-Brussels highway, trapping divisions west of Laon-Mons line. This resembled Patton's earlier envelopment, reinstating Montgomery's boundary, compressing British into Schelde zone. Bradley ordered Hodges without higher consultation. Objective Tournai, with 48-hour deadline by midnight 2 September, motivated by flank threat and opposing airborne drop on 3 September, aiming to prove ground forces sufficient.

6.Sub-event_summary: Hodges believed the speed was for linking with paratroopers on 3 September. Corlett motorized regiments using support unit trucks for 79th and 30th Divisions, led by 2d Armored Division, bypassing resistance. CCA crossed Somme on 1 September, reached Tournai by 2 September before deadline, with divisions assembling. Minimal resistance encountered, bridges built standardly. Incursion into British zone protested, but continued; halted at Tournai due to gasoline shortage while British advanced beyond. Processed 1,300 prisoners with captured fuel for mopping up.

9.Sub-event_summary: VII Corps ordered 31 August to turn north through Avesnes, Maubeuge, Mons, addressing gap with Third Army using reinforced 4th Cavalry Group, aiming for Meuse bridgehead near Mézières. Swerved 3d Armored from Sedan-Charleville to Hirson-Vervins, with 9th Division protecting flank, 1st reinforcing. 3d Armored reached near Mons by 2 September nightfall, columns stretched to Avesnes. Hodges unable to halt due to communication, took Mons morning 3 September. 9th at Charleroi, 1st pushing to Avesnes.
